Plan review BLOCKED, and the reviewer was right on all three findings. I verified them against the tree before editing.

The plan claimed validate and Finding must both stay importable from rebar._cli._registry because test_capabilities, test_cli_registry and test_cli_registry_dispatch all import them from there. False in specifics: test_capabilities and test_cli_registry import Route, validate; test_cli_registry_dispatch imports the module handle (from rebar._cli import _execute, _registry, main). None of the three imports Finding, and NOTHING in the tree imports Finding from rebar._cli._registry — the only Finding import anywhere is from the unrelated check_ssm_secret_state module.

Replaced the assumption with a census. 22 files reference rebar._cli._registry; across named imports and module-handle attribute access they consume exactly eight names: ROUTES, Route, validate, route_for, derive_policy_sets, ADAPTER_KINDS, INIT_POLICIES, KNOWN_CAPABILITIES. Of the cluster being moved only validate is externally consumed, so only validate needs the back-compat re-export; Finding is the cluster own return type and moves with it. AC2 now asserts those eight names resolve on the module after the split, which is a stronger and checkable postcondition than the three-test claim it replaces.

Worth noting for anyone repeating the census: my first scoped grep undercounted, because it matched "from rebar._cli import _registry" exactly and missed the dispatch test importing three names on one line. The 22-file figure comes from a pattern covering all three import shapes.

Re-review started.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Implemented and pushed as Gerrit change 2550 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2550), from a worktree off origin/main.

AC1: _registry.py 800 -> 685 lines (115 headroom); it no longer appears in the >780 near-cap census at all. AC4: _registry_checks.py is 170 lines, above the 100-line floor.

AC2: an __all__ in _registry.py pins the eight externally-consumed names from the census (ROUTES, Route, validate, route_for, derive_policy_sets, ADAPTER_KINDS, INIT_POLICIES, KNOWN_CAPABILITIES). Two mutations verify it: removing Finding from __all__ fails test_declared_surface_covers_the_split_names, and dropping the Finding re-export import fails test_public_surface_resolves with the exact missing name.

AC3/AC5: behaviour identical. Snapshotted route names, aliases, all 17 derived policy sets, validate() findings and the three vocabularies from the UNMODIFIED pre-split tree (a separate worktree at origin/main), then compared post-split: identical across all seven dimensions.

Design note on import direction, which the plan did not settle. A naive extraction cycles, because validate() defaults to ROUTES while the checks would live outside _registry. Resolved by keeping validate (and its default) in _registry and moving only the checks, which take the route table as a parameter — so _registry imports _registry_checks and never the reverse. Route is needed for annotations only, so it is imported under TYPE_CHECKING. The three vocabularies moved with the checks because the checks are their only runtime consumer (their other mentions in _registry were comments).

The committed test targets the failure mode an import-only test would miss: a check that moved but was left out of _CHECKS makes the registry validate CLEAN because the rule stopped running, not because the tree is good. So each of the nine rules is exercised independently through the public validate against a crafted violating table, plus a negative control. Dropping _check_capabilities from _CHECKS turns two tests red; dropping _check_execution turns five red.

Process note. During mutation testing I ran git checkout -- on _registry_checks.py while it was still UNTRACKED, so that revert silently failed; the next checkout then restored _registry.py to its pre-split state and wiped the split. I re-applied it, staged all three files first so reverts actually work, and re-ran the three mutations cleanly — the earlier __all__ result was contaminated by the unreverted first mutation and was discarded rather than reported.

Gates: make lint and make typecheck clean; 1127 passed / 3 skipped in tests/unit -k "registry or capabilities or dispatch or cli".

This unblocks F11 (elfin-decagonal-polarbear), which needs Route headroom.

compiled_state.description:
## Why this exists

`src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py` is at **exactly 800 lines** — the hard cap. Sibling
`elfin-decagonal-polarbear` (F11, mirror F11) must add a `warn_cross_session` flag to `Route`
and fold it into `derive_policy_sets`, which cannot be done without going over.

This is filed as its own ticket deliberately. Splitting a module is a structural change with
its own review surface; folding it into a mirror-remediation change would put an unrelated
refactor inside a change whose reviewed plan is about single-sourcing a policy set, and would
make both harder to review and to revert.

**This has already bitten this epic twice.** `_commands/composer.py` was likewise at exactly
800; the F3 change added an import and a comment, took the whole stack to `Verified -1`, and
the recovery mis-amended a commit and opened a duplicate Gerrit change. F7 then had to express
its fix in ZERO net lines to fit. That is code shaped around a cap rather than around meaning.

Four other `src/rebar` files sit at exactly 800 today (`llm/plan_review/sizing.py`,
`llm/plan_review/sidecar.py`, `_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py`,
`_commands/composer.py`), so this is a general hazard; this ticket addresses only the one the
epic is blocked on.

## The seam

Not a mechanical cut to hit a number. `_registry.py` holds three clusters, and one is already
self-contained:

- **route TABLE construction** — `_core_factory`, `_reads_init_only`, `_simple_read_groups`,
  `_lifecycle`, `_writes_full`, `_intercepts`, `_bridge_and_arms`, `_build_routes` (~520 lines)
- **types + lookup** — `Route`, `Finding`, `_index`, `route_for`, `derive_policy_sets`
- **registry VALIDATION** (`:684-795`, ~112 lines) — `_is_valid_reference`, the six `_check_*`
  functions, `_CHECKS`, `validate`

The validation cluster is the seam: its functions call only each other, take
`routes: tuple[Route, ...]` as a PARAMETER, and yield `Finding`. It reads the registry; it does
not build it. Extracting it leaves `_registry.py` at roughly 688 with ~112 lines of headroom,
and the new module lands well above the 100-LOC floor, so this is a split along an existing
call-graph seam rather than one invented for the cap.

The consumer surface is verified rather than assumed. 22 files reference
`rebar._cli._registry`, and across named imports and module-handle access they consume exactly
eight names: `ROUTES`, `Route`, `validate`, `route_for`, `derive_policy_sets`, `ADAPTER_KINDS`,
`INIT_POLICIES`, `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`. Of the cluster being moved, only `validate` is consumed
from outside, so `validate` must stay importable from `rebar._cli._registry`. `Finding` is
consumed NOWHERE outside the module — it is the validation cluster's own return type, named
only by the `_check_*` functions that move with it — so it needs no re-export. (`test_capabilities`
and `test_cli_registry` import `Route, validate`; `test_cli_registry_dispatch` imports the module
handle. None of the three imports `Finding`.) The in-tree precedent for the back-compat
re-export is `gate_dispatch.py`, which re-exports the `plan_review_recovery` cluster and
documents the re-export as load-bearing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: the validation cluster moves to a new `src/rebar/_cli/_registry_checks.py`, and
      `_registry.py` is under the cap with real headroom. Verified by `wc -l` on both and by the
      CI module-size gate passing.
- [x] AC2: the eight externally-consumed names remain resolvable on `rebar._cli._registry`
      after the split. Verified by a test that asserts each of `ROUTES`, `Route`, `validate`,
      `route_for`, `derive_policy_sets`, `ADAPTER_KINDS`, `INIT_POLICIES` and
      `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES` is present on the module, and by the existing consumer suites
      (`test_capabilities`, `test_cli_registry`, `test_cli_registry_dispatch`) passing
      untouched.
- [x] AC3: behavior is byte-identical — the same findings, in the same order, for the same
      routes. Verified by a test asserting `tuple(validate(ROUTES))` is unchanged and by
      `validate()` still returning empty on the committed registry.
- [x] AC4: the new module is above the 100-LOC floor, so this is a seam extraction and not a
      fragment. Verified by `wc -l`.
- [x] AC5: no route definition, alias, or policy set is altered. Verified by a test asserting
      the `ROUTES` name/alias sets and every `derive_policy_sets` output are identical to
      before, so the split cannot have moved behavior.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit -k "registry or capabilities or dispatch or cli" -q` — AC2, AC3,
  AC5 and the existing registry suites.
- `wc -l src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py src/rebar/_cli/_registry_checks.py` — AC1, AC4.
- `make lint && make typecheck`.
